body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26399

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/2490

## What I did

Investigated the reported v0.5.12 EAGLE verify path and the prepared `main` implementation. The reported source synchronously converts `accept_index`, `predict`, and accepted-length tensors to Python lists inside `EagleVerifyInput.verify`. Current `main` already contains the relevant correction: `run_eagle_verify` returns GPU tensors, and `GenerationBatchResult.copy_to_cpu` stages speculative token IDs and `accept_lens` through pinned nonblocking D2H copies. This behavior traces to https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29075.

No duplicate runtime change was justified. This PR adds a regression that:

- rejects `.cpu()`, `.tolist()`, or `.numpy()` in the current EAGLE verify hot path;
- executes the real ROCm GPU-to-pinned-host result-copy path;
- checks exact values for a multi-request speculative result;
- covers the empty-result boundary independently.

The investigation report and machine-readable result are under `reports/j-f2862992c228/` with outcome `candidate_verified`.

## Reproduce

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python \
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-f2862992c228/venv/bin/python \
  -m pytest -q test/registered/spec/test_eagle_verify_result_d2h.py
```

Result on the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X / gfx950: `3 passed`.

## Limitations

I could not reproduce or rule out the full production hang because the environment has one gfx950 rather than 8×H200 and does not contain GLM-5.1 FP8 weights. Therefore TP8 topology, CUDA/H200 behavior, 80K–160K prompts, near-full KV pressure, model semantics, and the watchdog failure remain unverified. On HIP the scheduler intentionally performs the pinned async copy on the forward stream, so this run validates removal of Python-side verify `.tolist()` calls and D2H value correctness, not CUDA copy-stream overlap.
